finding: A fixed-charge force field reproduces DENSITY acceptably but systematically UNDERESTIMATES the static dielectric constant (11/12 systems low, mean error -3.905). That is the expected physics: without explicit induced polarisation the model cannot produce the collective dipole response, so the computed epsilon collapses toward 1 for non-polar liquids and badly misses polar ones.

consequence_for_this_round.why: the physics RQ3 asks about (intermolecular dipole correlation contributing to epsilon) requires a force field that reproduces epsilon. The available fixed-charge layer does not, and no validated polarizable / Drude / fluctuating-charge parametrisation for these solvents is installed (openmm present, openff-evaluator/mdtraj/parmed absent, no polarizable FF shipped).
what_is_legitimate: report the fixed-charge MD as evidence that non-polarizable models fail on the dielectric response (a NEGATIVE control, not a result)
use the MD densities as a structural check only
what_is_NOT_legitimate: quoting eps_md as a predicted dielectric constant
using g_K from these runs to explain g_apparent
claiming a Kirkwood comparison was performed

next_step_if_resources_allow: install a validated polarizable model (e.g. AMOEBA/Drude via OpenMM or a fluctuating-charge scheme), re-run 4 systems, and require T1+T2 both pass before any mechanism claim
